name: La Paz
tagline: Cable cars above an Andean bowl
summary: La Paz rewards slow exploration through markets, viewpoints and its cable-car network. Build an easy arrival day into this high-altitude stop.
seasonNote: Dry winter offers clearer views but cold nights; summer rain can affect excursions.
arrival: LPB is at El Alto above the city; use an arranged transfer and pace your first day.
gettingAround: Use Mi Teleférico for views and selected connections; taxis help with steep cross-town journeys.
cashTip: Carry small boliviano notes and confirm ATM/card availability; avoid changing money with strangers.
foodTip: Try a freshly baked salteña in the morning and ask about meat or vegetarian fillings.
buyTip: Choose textiles and craft with clear provenance; do not buy wildlife or ritual animal products.
baseArea: Sopocachi or central accommodation with arranged transfers.

connections.note: Approximate long transfer; better split with Puno/Copacabana and verify border arrangements.
Approximate direct air time when scheduled; connections may be needed.

reviewSummary: Visitor listings highlight the cable-car and market experience; Calle Sagárnaga has an indexed 4.2/5 snapshot from 936 reviews. Treat Uyuni as a separate multi-day extension.

items.name: Mi Teleférico panorama ride
items.summary: Ride the urban cable cars for sweeping views and a different view of daily life.
items.expect: A functioning commuter network with multiple lines and transfers.
items.tip: Choose a short loop in daylight and ask staff about the right tickets.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate for several urban cable-car rides; confirm current tariff.

whyVisit: Cable cars reveal the city’s steep bowl and neighbourhoods from above.
The system is everyday public transport as well as a memorable way to see La Paz.

Ride the selected lines while leaving space for commuters.
items.bestFor: City orientation with minimal steep walking

items.name: Valle de la Luna
items.summary: Eroded clay formations create a sculptural landscape near the city.
items.expect: Short exposed paths with uneven edges; combine with a southern-district visit.
items.tip: Take sun protection and use proper footwear.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult; check the current official price.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Erosion has shaped clay into a compact landscape of pillars and gullies.

Walk slowly on uneven edges and pause at the main formations.
items.bestFor: Unusual geology on a shorter outing
items.tradeoffs: Short exposed paths with uneven edges; combine with a southern-district visit.

dayClusters.label: An easy cable-car introduction
dayClusters.note: Start with breakfast, then a short cable-car loop. Keep this first high-altitude day light and use vehicles rather than adding strenuous uphill walks.

dayClusters.label: Historic streets and the market quarter
dayClusters.note: Explore Calle Jaen and central museums, then the San Francisco/Sagarnaga area. Walk in daylight and leave room for steep streets and museum opening times.

dayClusters.label: Tiwanaku day excursion
dayClusters.note: Reserve a full day for arranged transport, the archaeological grounds and museums. Confirm the pickup, admission and return arrangements before departure.

dayClusters.label: Optional southern-city landscape
dayClusters.note: Valle de la Luna is an alternative shorter outing if you prefer to skip the long Tiwanaku excursion, or an additional day. Allow transport to Mallasa and an unhurried return.
